new_statements.quote: England 1990 p.221: 'Se ha acostumbrado a hablar, por lo menos, de las diferencias entre el Mam del norte, que abarca los pueblos de habla Mam de Huehuetenango y otros al norte del departamento de San Marcos, y el Mam del sur, que cubre el resto de San Marcos y la parte Mam de Quetzaltenango.' p.225: 'En Tacaná, el acento cae en la última sílaba, con la excepción de algunos enclíticos que nunca llevan acento (Munson 1984). ... En Ostuncalco el acento cae en la penúltima sílaba, y otra vez hay enclíticos que no tienen ningún efecto sobre la acentuación.' Godfrey & Collins 1987 p.100: 'El mam de Tajumulco, junto con el de Ixchiguán, se agrupa con los dialectos del sur.'
new_statements.translation: England p.221: 'It has been customary to speak, at least, of the differences between Northern Mam, which takes in the Mam-speaking towns of Huehuetenango and others in the north of the department of San Marcos, and Southern Mam, which covers the rest of San Marcos and the Mam part of Quetzaltenango.' p.225: 'In Tacaná, stress falls on the last syllable, except for some enclitics that never bear stress (Munson 1984). ... In Ostuncalco stress falls on the penultimate syllable, and again there are enclitics that have no effect on stress placement.' Godfrey & Collins p.100: 'The Mam of Tajumulco, together with that of Ixchiguán, groups with the southern dialects.'

new_statements.rule_in_words: No source states a stress rule for Tajumulco Mam by name. By England's regional division Tajumulco (San Marcos, not northern, not Tacaná/Sibinal) falls in Southern Mam, for which she states penultimate word stress with enclitics outside the stress domain (exemplar San Juan Ostuncalco); Godfrey & Collins independently group Tajumulco+Ixchiguán with the southern dialects, and their stress-marked Tajumulco transcriptions (Apéndice 6, points 54/55) are mostly penultimate where neighbouring Tacaná is final. Provisional reading: penultimate.
new_statements.exceptions: England: enclitics never bear stress and do not count (Tacaná and Ostuncalco alike). In the Godfrey & Collins Tajumulco data one token shows stress on a word-final long vowel (qčuyá·), so a residual weight effect cannot be excluded; Spanish loans keep Spanish stress (sabér, púro).
new_statements.domain_note: England's statements are word-level citation forms per town (Ostuncalco = south, Tacaná = west, Ixtahuacán = north); enclitics excluded from the domain. Godfrey & Collins p.20 warn their acute marks are phonetic stresses in connected sentences and 'may not coincide with the stress the word would carry in isolation'.
new_statements.identity_note: mamt1234 is a Glottolog bookkeeping code for the retired Ethnologue entry 'Mam, Tajumulco' [mpf] = the Mam of Tajumulco and Ixchiguán (San Marcos, Guatemala; the target record's 'MX' is wrong per Ethnologue 15), a dialect of Mam (mamm1241). The quoted stress statement is NOT about Tajumulco by name: England 1990 states penultimate stress for Southern Mam as exemplified by San Juan Ostuncalco (the variety of retired mms = mams1234) and defines Southern Mam as 'el resto de San Marcos y la parte Mam de Quetzaltenango', which territorially includes Tajumulco; Godfrey & Collins 1987 p.100 group Tajumulco+Ixchiguán with 'los dialectos del sur' (while also treating 'Mam tajumulteco' as its own literacy group, and López & Collins 1991 list Tajumulco under 'mam central', whose Comitancillo standard G&C describe as having 'la penúltima sílaba tónica'). The earlier scan's 'weight-sensitive' verdict came from England 1983 on Ixtahuacán (Northern Mam) and does not apply to Tajumulco. If catalogued, the entry should be flagged as a regional extrapolation (Southern Mam statement) pending Pérez et al. 2000 or England 2017.

sources.note: p.221: 'Mam del sur... cubre el resto de San Marcos y la parte Mam de Quetzaltenango' (Mam del norte = Huehuetenango + towns in the north of San Marcos; Mam occidental = Tacaná, Sibinal, part of Tectitán). sec. 1.2.3 Acento pp.225-226: Tacaná (west) final stress; Ostuncalco (south) penultimate, enclitics ignored; Ixtahuacán (north) heavy-syllable rule. Tajumulco is not named; it falls in 'el resto de San Marcos'.
